title: In silico evidence for gluconeogenesis from fatty acids in humans
authors: Kaleta C, de Figueiredo LF, Werner S, Guthke R, Ristow M, Schuster S

result: Computational study. Elementary flux pattern analysis of a genome-scale human metabolic network of 5733 reactions and 3188 metabolites found pathways that convert four acetyl-CoA into one glucose and two CO2 through acetoacetate, acetone and acetol, then methylglyoxal or D-lactaldehyde, to pyruvate. The pathways consume 6 to 22 ATP per glucose and require NADPH, which the authors argue limits their capacity. Fluxes were not measured experimentally.
